newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST-San Miguel 9-mth net 3.69 bln peso.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-San Miguel 9-mth net 3.69 bln peso.

text.p: Beer and food firm San Miguel Corp is expected to post net profit of 3.6914 in the first nine months of the year, unchanged from the year-ago figure, the average of a Reuter poll of eight stock brokers showed.
Last year, San Miguel reported a net profit of 3.69 billion pesos in the first nine months.

The poll completed on Monday predicted full year 1996 profits at 5.24 billion pesos, down from 1995 profits of 5.84 billion which was boosted by an extraordinary gain of 223 million pesos coming from an initial public offering by one of its liquor-making units.

"Earnings of San Miguel for the first nine months will not be spectacular. It's the same story. Their earnings are being eaten up by expansion abroad and higher interest expenses," Fritz Aclan, research head at Dharmala Securities (Phils) said.
San Miguel, the country's biggest beer firm and among the top 10 stocks in terms of market capitalisation, has done poorly this year.
For the first six months of 1996, it reported a profit of 2.4 billion pesos, 19 percent lower than the year-ago figure of 3.0 billion pesos.

"The last quarter is usually the better quarter for San Miguel. This last quarter will not be any different as a result of increased demand during the Christmas season," said Patrick Garcia, vice-president at L.M. Garcia & Associates.

SMC's softdrinks arm, Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc is also expected to boost the company's earnings. "We see a 12 percent growth in Coke sales for the first nine months compared to last year," said Kevin Khoe, analyst at Sapphire Securities Inc.
Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc said: "We are taking San Miguel's word for it, that growth in profits will contract for the whole year."

Last week, speaking at the Jardine Fleming Asia Conference in New York, San Miguel's Chief Financial Officer Delfin Gonzalez Jr said the firm expects third quarter income to show some improvement over last year.
However, this would not compensate for the shortfall of the first half and the company "expects to finish the year with net income slightly lower than last year," Gonzalez said.
